14: def index_labels(labels, case_sensitive=False):
15:     """Convert a list of string identifiers into numerical indices.
16: 
17:     Parameters
18:     ----------
19:     labels : list of strings, shape=(n,)
20:         A list of annotations, e.g., segment or chord labels from an
21:         annotation file.
22:     case_sensitive : bool
23:         Set to True to enable case-sensitive label indexing
24:         (Default value = False)
25: 
26:     Returns
27:     -------
28:     indices : list, shape=(n,)
29:         Numerical representation of ``labels``
30:     index_to_label : dict
31:         Mapping to convert numerical indices back to labels.
32:         ``labels[i] == index_to_label[indices[i]]``
33:     """
34:     label_to_index = {}
35:     index_to_label = {}
36: 
37:     # If we're not case-sensitive,
38:     if not case_sensitive:
39:         labels = [str(s).lower() for s in labels]
40: 
41:     # First, build the unique label mapping
42:     for index, s in enumerate(sorted(set(labels))):
43:         label_to_index[s] = index
44:         index_to_label[index] = s
45: 
46:     # Remap the labels to indices
47:     indices = [label_to_index[s] for s in labels]
48: 
49:     # Return the converted labels, and the inverse mapping
50:     return indices, index_to_label
51: 
52: 
53: def generate_labels(items, prefix="__"):
54:     """Given an array of items (e.g. events, intervals), create a synthetic label
55:     for each event of the form '(label prefix)(item number)'
56: 
57:     Parameters
58:     ----------
59:     items : list-like
60:         A list or array of events or intervals
61:     prefix : str
62:         This prefix will be prepended to all synthetically generated labels
63:         (Default value = '__')
64: 
65:     Returns
66:     -------
67:     labels : list of str
68:         Synthetically generated labels
69: 
70:     """
71:     return [f"{prefix}{n}" for n in range(len(items))]
72: 
73: 
74: def intervals_to_samples(intervals, labels, offset=0, sample_size=0.1, fill_value=None):
75:     """Convert an array of labeled time intervals to annotated samples.
76: 
77:     Parameters
78:     ----------
79:     intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, d)
80:         An array of time intervals, as returned by
81:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals()` or
82:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals()`.
83:         The ``i`` th interval spans time ``intervals[i, 0]`` to
84:         ``intervals[i, 1]``.
85:     labels : list, shape=(n,)
86:         The annotation for each interval
87:     offset : float > 0
88:         Phase offset of the sampled time grid (in seconds)
89:         (Default value = 0)
90:     sample_size : float > 0
91:         duration of each sample to be generated (in seconds)
92:         (Default value = 0.1)
93:     fill_value : type(labels[0])
94:         Object to use for the label with out-of-range time points.
95:         (Default value = None)
96: 
97:     Returns
98:     -------
99:     sample_times : list
100:         list of sample times
101:     sample_labels : list
102:         array of labels for each generated sample
103: 
104:     Notes
105:     -----
106:         Intervals will be rounded down to the nearest multiple
107:         of ``sample_size``.
108:     """
109:     # Round intervals to the sample size
110:     num_samples = int(np.floor(intervals.max() / sample_size))
111:     sample_indices = np.arange(num_samples, dtype=np.float32)
112:     sample_times = (sample_indices * sample_size + offset).tolist()
113:     sampled_labels = interpolate_intervals(intervals, labels, sample_times, fill_value)
114: 
115:     return sample_times, sampled_labels
116: 
117: 
118: def interpolate_intervals(intervals, labels, time_points, fill_value=None):
119:     """Assign labels to a set of points in time given a set of intervals.
120: 
121:     Time points that do not lie within an interval are mapped to `fill_value`.
122: 
123:     Parameters
124:     ----------
125:     intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
126:         An array of time intervals, as returned by
127:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals()`.
128:         The ``i`` th interval spans time ``intervals[i, 0]`` to
129:         ``intervals[i, 1]``.
130: 
131:         Intervals are assumed to be disjoint.
132: 
133:     labels : list, shape=(n,)
134:         The annotation for each interval
135: 
136:     time_points : array_like, shape=(m,)
137:         Points in time to assign labels.  These must be in
138:         non-decreasing order.
139: 
140:     fill_value : type(labels[0])
141:         Object to use for the label with out-of-range time points.
142:         (Default value = None)
143: 
144:     Returns
145:     -------
146:     aligned_labels : list
147:         Labels corresponding to the given time points.
148: 
149:     Raises
150:     ------
151:     ValueError
152:         If `time_points` is not in non-decreasing order.
153:     """
154:     # Verify that time_points is sorted
